trust_boundaries.notion_host: Authenticates the Second Brain subject, validates CSRF, resolves the canonical Notion workspace/page authority, and issues one ticket.
trust_boundaries.collaboration_gateway: Consumes one ticket and transports only versioned envelopes; a Flask cookie is never gateway authorization.
trust_boundaries.canonical_authority: Owns current membership, page role, workspace/page epochs, accepted operations, per-document event sequence, audit, and outbox.
trust_boundaries.client: Owns an untrusted client identifier and operation identifiers; it cannot assert roles, capabilities, epochs, or durable sequence.
trust_boundaries.second_brain: Shares authenticated subject identity only. Notion revisions, events, and authorization remain independent from immutable SBE publication revisions.

threats.attack: Cross-site ticket issuance through an authenticated browser.
threats.control: Issue only after the Notion host validates the authenticated session and CSRF token.

threats.attack: A ticket is copied to another origin, subject, workspace, page, client, or session.
threats.control: Bind every claim and require exact comparison during atomic one-time consumption.

threats.attack: A consumed or expired ticket is reused.
threats.control: Persist only its SHA-256 digest, burn a recognized ticket on its first consume attempt, and use one non-oracle rejection.

threats.attack: Envelope metadata or payload is modified in transit or during queueing.
threats.control: Validate the protocol version, exact binding, capability, byte length, and SHA-256 payload digest before admission.

threats.attack: Lost responses and retries apply one logical operation more than once.
threats.control: Deduplicate by subject, page, and caller operation ID; same request hash returns the original ACK and a different hash conflicts.

threats.attack: Out-of-order or skipped client sequence changes durable order.
threats.control: Accept only the next client sequence and allocate the document event sequence on durable commit.

threats.attack: Queued writes or replay deliver after membership or page permission changes.
threats.control: Bind workspace/page epochs and revalidate current authority at admission, replay, and immediately before protected send.

threat_model.non_oracle_rejection: Unknown, malformed, expired, reused, wrong-origin, wrong-binding, and stale-epoch tickets all return collaboration ticket rejected without protected identifiers or claims.

envelope_contract.validation_rule: Reject unknown versions/types, non-granted capabilities, binding drift, stale epochs, oversized payloads, byte-length drift, and payload hash drift before admission.

sequence_ack_replay_contract.client_sequence_rule: Exactly next per subject/page/client/session binding; gaps, unknown repeats, and sequence reuse fail closed.
sequence_ack_replay_contract.document_sequence_rule: Canonical authority allocates one monotonically increasing value only when the event becomes durable.
sequence_ack_replay_contract.same_operation_same_request: Return the original acknowledgement without another event or sequence allocation after current authorization revalidation.
sequence_ack_replay_contract.client_acknowledgement_rule: A client may acknowledge only a document sequence at or below the current durable high-water mark.
